blocks.h2: Is Your Arlington Heights Gas Fireplace Acting Up?
blocks.intro: These are the calls we get most when it gets cold:

tiles.body: Dust and debris in the pilot after a summer off are the usual cause.
A worn thermocouple or thermopile can no longer hold the gas valve open.

tiles.h3: Black Glass or a Yellow Flame
tiles.body: A dirty burner, logs out of place or a venting problem.
Leave the house. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, then call us once it's safe.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Repair, Cleaning and Yearly Service

steps.body: Pilot assemblies, igniters, thermocouples, thermopiles, gas valves, remotes and wall switches.
We clean the burner, pilot and glass, reset the logs, leak-test the connections and check the vent.
Converting a wood fireplace to gas logs or adding an insert? See [gas line installation](/arlington-heights/gas-line-installation).

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplaces in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: Fireplaces here reflect when each home was built.

items.body: Many homes from the 1950s through the 1970s have brick fireplaces that got gas logs later. The damper has to stay open and the flue has to be clear. We check the gas side and tell you if the chimney needs attention.
A gas insert vents through a liner in the old chimney. A damaged liner can push exhaust back into the room.
Direct-vent fireplaces from the 1980s are now 37 to 46 years old. Most parts can still be replaced without replacing the unit.
Keep a working CO detector on every level and near any gas appliance.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How often should a gas fireplace be serviced?
items.preview: Once a year, before heating season.
items.answer: Once a year, ideally in September or October, so any weak part shows up before the first cold night.

items.q: Why won't my fireplace light after summer?
items.preview: Dust and debris in the pilot.
items.answer: Dust and debris build up in the pilot tube and burner over the summer. A cleaning usually fixes it. If not, the thermocouple or thermopile is the next suspect.

items.q: Can gas logs go in my old wood-burning fireplace?
items.preview: Often, if the chimney is sound and a gas line can reach it.
items.answer: Often, yes. The chimney needs to be in good shape and drawing well, and a gas line has to be run to the firebox. We handle the gas line and tell you if anything needs a chimney professional first.

items.q: What should I do if I smell gas near my fireplace?
items.preview: Leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
items.answer: Leave the house and don't touch any switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, then call us once it's safe.

items.q: How much does gas fireplace repair cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on what failed. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the part that failed and the make of the fireplace. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
